poiseuille_channel.title: Plane Poiseuille flow (laminar channel)
poiseuille_channel.description: Laminar flow of a fluid with ν = 1e-5 m²/s between two parallel plates 0.1 m apart, 2 m long, mean velocity 0.01 m/s (Re = 100).
poiseuille_channel.reference: Analytical: u(y) = 6·U·(y/H)(1 − y/H), dp/dx = −12 ν U / H²

poiseuille_pipe.title: Hagen–Poiseuille flow (laminar pipe, axisymmetric)
poiseuille_pipe.description: Laminar flow in a circular pipe of radius 5 cm and length 2 m, mean velocity 0.01 m/s, ν = 1e-5 m²/s (Re_D = 100).
poiseuille_pipe.reference: Analytical: u(r) = 2·U·(1 − r²/R²), dp/dx = −8 ν U / R²

cavity_ra1e5.title: Natural convection in a square cavity, Ra = 10⁵
cavity_ra1e5.description: Natural convection of air in a square cavity of side 4.59 cm, hot left wall at 305 K, cold right wall at 295 K, adiabatic top and bottom (Ra = 1e5). Steady state, laminar.
cavity_ra1e5.reference: de Vahl Davis, Int. J. Numer. Meth. Fluids 3 (1983) 249–264
cavity_ra1e5.notes: Compressible perfect-gas solver with ΔT = 10 K (≈ Boussinesq); uniform 100 × 100 mesh; the reference is a Boussinesq solution at Pr = 0.71 (case: Pr = 0.713).

Max v on horizontal centreline · L/α

cylinder_re100.title: Vortex shedding behind a circular cylinder, Re = 100
cylinder_re100.description: Laminar flow past a 2-D circular cylinder at Re = 100 (D = 1 m, U = 1 m/s, ν = 0.01 m²/s), in a domain 30 D long and 20 D high with the cylinder 10 D from the inlet. Transient; measure the vortex-shedding frequency.
cylinder_re100.reference: Williamson, Annu. Rev. Fluid Mech. 28 (1996): St = 0.2665 − 1.018/√Re
cylinder_re100.notes: Symmetry planes 10 D above and below the cylinder (5 % blockage) raise St slightly compared with an unbounded flow. The period is measured from zero crossings of u_y at a probe 2 D behind the cylinder.

backstep_driver.title: Turbulent backward-facing step (Driver & Seegmiller)
backstep_driver.description: Air at 44.2 m/s flows over a backward-facing step 1.27 cm high; the channel is 8 step heights high upstream and 9 downstream. Steady, turbulent (k-omega SST).
backstep_driver.reference: Driver & Seegmiller, AIAA J. 23 (1985) 163–171: x_r / H = 6.26 ± 0.10
backstep_driver.notes: RANS models predict reattachment less precisely than laminar flows (k-ε typically under-predicts it by 15–20 %), hence the ±10 % tolerance. Uniform inflow developed over ≈ 80 H of channel; wall functions on wall-graded cells. Mesh sensitivity: 23 600 → 42 100 cells changes x_r / H by 1.3 % (5.96 → 6.04), so the deviation comes from the turbulence model, not the mesh.

cylinder_re40.title: Steady wake behind a circular cylinder, Re = 40
cylinder_re40.description: Steady laminar flow past a 2-D circular cylinder at Re = 40 (D = 1 m, U = 1 m/s, ν = 0.025 m²/s), in a domain 30 D long and 20 D high with the cylinder 10 D from the inlet. Measure the length of the recirculation bubble behind it.
cylinder_re40.reference: Dennis & Chang, J. Fluid Mech. 42 (1970); Fornberg, J. Fluid Mech. 98 (1980); Coutanceau & Bouard, J. Fluid Mech. 79 (1977): L_w/D = 2.13–2.35
cylinder_re40.notes: Below the shedding threshold (Re ≈ 47) the wake is steady. The literature spread (2.13–2.35) sets the ±10 % tolerance; symmetry planes 10 D away (5 % blockage). Also run with code_saturne (validation/compare.py).
